title: Customer Insights Sprint: Preflight Checklist & Decision Heuristics (Draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for a short-form "customer insights sprint" — a focused meeting that combines a QBR-style health check with a decision lab to produce 1–2 concrete renewal/expansion asks and an action plan. Goal: leave the meeting with an explicit decision (renew/expand/execute-safety-plan) and the owner(s) and timeline for the next 90 days.

When to use this vs a full QBR:
- Use when the account shows usage signals but there are open adoption questions, or when renewal is within 90 days and we need quick alignment.
- Not for first-touch onboarding reviews or very large strategic exec reviews.

Attendees & Roles (30–75 minute meeting template):
- CSM (facilitator / decision scribe): owns agenda, runs timebox, records decisions.
- Customer success manager (partner): brings adoption context and next-steps.
- Customer product owner (business stakeholder): decision-maker or influencer.
- Customer engineering/ops (optional): for technical blockers.
- Redwood solutions engineer or AE (optional): for product/contract questions.
- Note: keep attendee list tight — default 5 people max.

Preflight data checklist (2–4 business days before):
- Usage snapshot (CSM): last 90/30/7 day token usage, request rate, top endpoints (who, what). Owner: CSM.
- Error & latency summary (SRE/observability): incidents in last 90 days, P99 latency shifts, any capacity warnings. Owner: Observability team link or SRE contact.
- Feature adoption signals (Product): embeddings, reranking, function-calls usage, routes with degraded quality. Owner: Product analyst.
- Support triage (Support): open high-severity tickets, escalations, time-to-first-response. Owner: Support lead.
- Financial snapshot (AE/Finance): current ARR, upcoming contract end date, NRR-impacting line items (discounts, credits). Owner: AE.
- Prepare 1–2 exemplar prompts/conversations (CSM + SE) that show quality issues or wins to demo live.
- Send pre-read to attendees 48 hours prior (one-pager + 3 charts).

Meeting agenda (60 minutes — adjust to 45/90 as needed):
- 0:00–0:05 — Welcome & outcomes (CSM)
  - Script: "Thanks all. Goal: agree on a renewal posture and 90-day plan with owners. We’ll surface risks and commit to next actions."
- 0:05–0:15 — Current-state health highlights (CSM + product one-slide)
  - Quick charts: usage trend, success rate, latency, top routes. Call out any regressions or outsized costs.
- 0:15–0:30 — Customer outcomes & blockers (Customer PO speaks; CSM prompts)
  - Facilitation cue: "What are the business outcomes you measure? Where are we helping/hurting?"
- 0:30–0:45 — Live exemplar walkthrough (SE + CSM)
  - Show 1 success and 1 failure prompt; capture observed gaps. Keep demo <8 minutes.
- 0:45–0:55 — Decision lab (facilitated)
  - Present the decision heuristics (see below). Use voting if disagreement. Capture decision and confidence score.
- 0:55–1:00 — Next steps & owners (scribe records)
  - Confirm 90-day plan, owners, and date for follow-up check-in (30d checkpoint).

Facilitation script snippets (bite-sized):
- Opening: "We’ll keep this tight — 60 minutes and one decision. If something needs deeper engineering time we’ll create a follow-up session."
- Risk framing: "There are three things that cause the most renewal friction: performance/cost surprises, unmet business metrics, and integration/ops incidents. Which of these hit you hardest?"
- When tension: "Let’s map the tradeoff: what happens if we keep current config vs if we implement the proposed change?"

Decision heuristics (use these to converge quickly):
- Confidence lever (0–100): team consensus on solution quality and runbook readiness.
- Business impact (Low / Medium / High): based on direct KPIs (e.g., conversions, time saved).
- Effort & risk (S / M / L): cross-team implementation cost, infra risk, data migration.
- Renewal trigger mapping:
  - If Business impact = High AND Confidence >= 60 => Recommend Expand / Upsell conversation.
  - If Business impact = Medium AND Confidence >= 50 => Recommend Renew with commit to 30-day proof-of-progress.
  - If Business impact = Low OR Confidence < 40 => Recommend Safety Plan (short-term credits, technical remediation, 30d checkpoint).

Quick scoring template (facilitator fills live):
- Business impact: "Medium"
- Confidence lever: "55"
- Effort & risk: "M"
- Recommended posture: "Renew + 30d proof-of-progress"

Renewal triggers & action mappings (operational table in prose):
- Drop in core KPI > 20% month-over-month => route to SE + Product for triage; schedule hot follow-up within 7 days.
- P99 latency increase > 2x baseline + elevated error rate => SRE-led incident review and temporary throttling/route-failover recommendations.
- Declining token usage but rising cost per call => propose quantization/experiment + cost forecast within 14 days.

Post-meeting deliverables (48–72 hours):
- 1–page decision memo (CSM): summary decision, rationale, owners, and metrics to watch.
- Action tracker (sheet link): owners, due dates, acceptance criteria.
- Follow-up booking (30d checkpoint) — calendar invite with pre-reads.

Notes to self (working items / TODOs):
- Add a lightweight Miro decision board template for voting next iteration.
- Ask Product to produce a short playbook for common regression signatures (embedding drift, reranking drop).
- Confirm observability dashboard permission for customer PO before meeting.

Open questions / discussion items (for reviewers):
- Should we require SE presence for all renewal windows under $50k ARR? Pros/cons.
- Is the Confidence lever too fuzzy? Consider 0–10 scale and anchor examples.

Parking lot (non-decision items we will log and follow up):
- Long-term roadmap ask (product backlog request)
- Pricing re-structuring conversation (escalate to AE + Rev Ops if triggered)

Appendix: quick pre-read checklist to attach to invite (copy into calendar invite)
- One-pager: health snapshot + ask (1 page)
- Top 3 data visuals: 90d usage trend, P99 latency, support tickets by severity
- Two live examples: good and bad prompt (so we can demo)

Version notes: this is a compact, bias-for-action variant of our standard account review. Meant to produce a binary-ish decision and clear owner path for follow-through. Feedback welcome — tag in doc comments or ping me in #cs-engagements.

-- Asha
